answer: Running 66 aliases as a result means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden honest agents do not face at scale. Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the tundra schedule in the zenith ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the lagoon checkpoint releases it only after review. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 3 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. That is 40 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
